newsitem.title: UK: Stakis confident about coming years.
newsitem.headline: Stakis confident about coming years.

text.p: Scottish-based Stakis Plc said on Monday that it was confident about the long-term prospects for its hotel, casino and leisure club divisions.
"We have a clear strategy to develop three businesses whose markets are expected to be buoyant in the middle term," chief executive David Michels said in a statement.

"We have a management team capable of delivering growth in all those businesses. We have adequate and prudent financing for that growth. I look forward to the next few years with confidence and enthusiasm," he added. Stakis lifted annual pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit 24 percent to 30.7 million stg.

The results for the year to end-September were in line with a forecast made by the company five weeks ago when it announced it was buying five Metropole hotels in the UK from Lonrho Plc for 327 million stg.
The deal is being largely funded by a four-for-seven rights issue, at 82 pence per share, which will raise 222 million stg.
The acquisition will increase the value of the group by nearly 50 percent. Gearing goes up to 45 percent after the purchase, from 38 percent at year-end.
Stakis said operating profit from its hotel division, 45-strong before the deal, rose 29 percent to 40.2 million stg.
Better occupancy rates and higher charges per room helped boost the division. New hotels are being built in London, Sheffield, Dublin and Belfast.
"Our three main markets - Corporate UK, UK Holidays and overseas visitors - continue to rise steadily year-on-year," Michels said.

Profits from the company's 22 casinos fell by 2.8 million stg to 8.9 million, a result which the company said was "disappointing". But it added that a review had identified this business as having great potential and Stakis intends to focus on provincial operations in the UK.
It sold its Barracuda Casino in London in April and is in the process of locating sites for six new provincial casinos which will open in the next two years.
Michels said the company believed the performance of the division was probably turning around.
"We have achieved a great deal in the past six months and we remain committed to the casino division although it will be some time before we can realise its full potential," he said.
The Health and Leisure Division made a first financial contribution of 600,000 stg.
The company said it was aiming for a rapid expansion of its LivingWell health club brand and said that it had already identified several sites which could be developed.
